facts.statement: Kamuysaurus was a herbivorous hadrosaurid dinosaur found in Late Cretaceous marine deposits near Mukawa, Hokkaido, Japan.
facts.quote: Kamuysaurus is a genus of herbivorous edmontosaurin saurolophine hadrosaurid dinosaur from Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) marine deposits of the Yezo Group (Hakobuchi Formation) in the Hobetsu area near the town of Mukawa, Hokkaido in Japan.

facts.statement: An amateur paleontologist discovered the tail of a euornithopod at Shirafunezawa Creek in 2003.
facts.quote: In 2003, amateur paleontologist Yoshiyuki Horita at the Shirafunezawa Creek discovered the tail of a euornithopod.

facts.statement: An entire skeleton was uncovered by museum teams in 2013 and 2014.
facts.quote: An entire skeleton was in 2013 and 2014 uncovered by teams of the Hobetsu Museum and the Hokkaido University Museum.

facts.statement: The species Kamuysaurus japonicus was named and described in 2019 by a team led by Professor Yoshitsugu Kobayashi.
facts.quote: In 2019, the type species Kamuysaurus japonicus was named and described by Professor Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Tomohiro Nishimura, Ryuji Takasaki, Kentaro Chiba, Anthony Ricardo Fiorillo, Kohei Tanaka, Tsogtbaatar Chinzorig, Tamaki Sato and Kazuhiko Sakurai.

facts.statement: The holotype represents an adult individual at least nine years old.
facts.quote: The holotype represents an adult individual of at least nine years of age.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the carcass was likely washed into the sea.
facts.quote: It was likely washed into the sea as a carcass.

facts.statement: Its weight is estimated at 4 or 5.3 tonnes, depending on whether it was bipedal or quadrupedal.
facts.quote: From the width of its thighbone, its weight has been estimated at 4 or 5.3 t, dependent on its having been bipedal or quadrupedal respectively.

facts.statement: The describing authors identified three unique derived characters, or autapomorphies, for the species.
facts.quote: Three of these were autapomorphies, unique derived characters.

facts.statement: A unique feature is a notch on the quadrate bone located at three-quarters of the shaft length from the top.
facts.quote: On the quadrate bone, the notch at the opening separating it from the quadratojugal bone, is located at a very low position, at three quarters of the shaft length measured from the top of the element.

facts.statement: Neural spines on the sixth through thirteenth back vertebrae are inclined forward.
facts.quote: The sixth tot thirteenth back vertebrae have neural spines that are inclined to the front.

facts.statement: The position of the notch on the quadrate bone is unique among all Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: This is unique for the Hadrosauridae as a whole.

facts.statement: Kamuysaurus belongs to the subfamily Hadrosaurinae.
Kamuysaurus is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
Kamuysaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
The time range for the genus is listed as the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
